    The wires

    Every wire is cut from the jumper wires in your set: thin stranded copper in plastic insulation, with a crimped end in a small black housing at each end. Where a wire is soldered, that end is cut off and stripped. Where it pushes onto a pin, that end is kept, and it must be a female end (the one with a hole). Use 20 cm jumpers or longer. Jumper wire carries the motor's current (a few tenths of an amp) without trouble here.

    Soldering

    The joints, by place

    • Battery contacts: 2 joints, 4 wire ends, on the bench (step 7).
    • XIAO battery pads: 2 joints, in the case (step 10).
    • AS5600 board: 5 holes, 7 wire ends, on the bench (step 14).

    How to make each joint

    1. Iron at about 330 °C. Tin the tip: melt a little solder on it and wipe it, so it is shiny.
    2. Strip 2 to 3 mm, twist the strands tight, and tin them: iron under, solder on top until it soaks in.
    3. On a flat pad (XIAO): melt a small bump on the pad, lay the wire on it, iron on the wire 2 to 3 s, lift, hold still 3 s.
    4. In a plated hole (AS5600): wire through from the side without the chip, iron on the ring and wire together, feed solder until the hole fills with a small cone. Trim afterwards.
    5. On a contact's tab: tin the tab first (piece out of the bay), then wires on it, 1 to 2 s.
    6. Check: smooth and shiny, flowing onto both. A dull ball did not flow: heat again. Nothing joining two pads. A gentle pull.

    Tools

    • The 60 W iron, fine pointed tip; 63/37 rosin core solder, 0.8 across; a damp sponge or brass wool.
    • Multimeter, flush cutters, wire strippers, a fine pen, flat-nosed pliers, electrical tape, a cloth, a vice or block (step 14), the M3 screwdriver and hex key.

    Safety

    • No cells in the bay while you solder.
    • 63/37 solder contains lead: keep air moving, don't eat while soldering, wash your hands afterwards.
    • The tip is about 330 °C. Back in its stand every time you let go of it.
    • Do the meter checks (steps 10 and 12) before the first cells go in. A swapped + and − can damage the XIAO.
    • Whenever USB-C is plugged into the XIAO, take one cell out first: its charger would try to charge the AA cells, which can make them leak.
    • Never 4 cells (about 6.4 V, over the battery pads' 6 V limit), and never the XIAO's 5V pin.

    AS5600 board

    Why this order

    1. A part goes in before anything that covers it. The battery bay covers the most: the motor's lower screw (behind the boss that carries the sensor bridge), the ULN2003's two lower screws, most of the motor's plug, the cable coil, and the step wires' route.
    2. A wire is cut only once both of its ends' places are fixed. Where one end is soldered on the bench (the battery contacts, the sensor board), the wire is first laid along its real route in the case and marked.
    3. The XIAO's battery pads come last in their area. A pad can tear off its board, so they're soldered once the bay is screwed down and nothing after pulls on them.
    4. Until the cover goes on, the base is open on all four sides above its lip (25 from the wall), so the ULN2003's pins can be reached over the top lip, and the XIAO from the bottom through the lip's notch.

    Why the battery wires aren't threaded through the slot

    The only way from the slot to the front is the plate's own pocket. So the wires are soldered to the tab's end at the bay's back instead (step 7).

    Still to check on the real parts

    • Which ULN2003 power pin is + (step 2).
    • That the contacts fit their pockets, and their tabs show in the recesses (step 7).
    • The XIAO's battery pad labels, against Seeed's pinout (step 10).
    • That the AS5600 board matches its listing picture, and whether two wires fit one hole (step 14).
    • The ULN2003, the motor cable and the contacts are placed from photo estimates, so routes and openings here are estimates too. The allowances in steps 6 and 13 cover a route up to about 10 longer.

    The 3D model, the pictures and the drawings are made from the case model by cad/wall_case/v6.6/soldering_guide_model.py (run it from hardware/cad after any change). Wire routes are the hand-routed estimates in wall_case_v6.6.py.

    Why now: once the bay is in, the boss on its right side stands right in front of the motor's lower screw.

    1. Motor into its collar, body flat on the floor, wire housing pointing left.
    2. 2 × M3 × 8 through its tabs. Snug, not hard: the post walls beside the motor are 1.0 thick.

    Why now: its two lower screws end up under the bay.

    1. Board onto its four posts: motor socket at the bottom, IN pins along the top.
    2. 4 × M3 × 8 through the corner holes.
    3. Read the print by the power pins and note which is +. Leave the jumper cap on.

    Why now: the bay covers most of the socket and all of the coil.

    1. Push the motor's plug into the white socket. It fits one way round.
    2. Coil the rest of the cable flat, about 22 × 34 and no more than 8 high. Tape it.
    3. Lay the coil on the floor, left of the motor.

    Why now: nothing is round it yet, and every wire to it is then cut to its real place.

    1. XIAO into its pocket: pins up, USB-C end against the bottom wall.
    2. XIAO clamp v1 over it, 2 × M3 × 8.
    3. Push a USB-C plug in and pull it out: the board must not move.

    Why now: they run behind the bay, from the ULN2003 above it to the XIAO below it.

    1. Take 4 whole jumpers. Nothing to cut.
    2. Push one end's sockets onto IN1 to IN4.
    3. Lead them down over the coil, between the bay's two lower posts, to the XIAO.
    4. Check each reaches its pin (D7 to D10) with about 10 to spare. Fold the rest flat on the coil and tape it.
    5. Leave the XIAO ends off its pins, to the right of the XIAO, until step 11.

    Why now: they're soldered to the battery contacts on the bench in step 7, so their length is found first, along their real route.

    Hands: the bay's posts mark its corners. Hold the wires at the posts' height, not down on the floor.

    1. Wire 2, red: socket onto the ULN2003's + pin. Lead it to the top left post. Pen mark at the post's edge nearest the cells.
    2. Wire 4, black: socket onto the − pin. Lead it down, left of the step wires, to the bottom right post. Pen mark at that post's edge.
    3. Cut each 15 past its mark and strip 3. Pull both sockets off.
    4. Wires 1 and 3: a whole jumper each, both ends cut off. Leave them long.

    Why on the bench: each joint sits in a recess in the bay's back, which faces the wall once the bay is in.

    1. Have the 4 metal pieces: a + single, a − single, 2 linked.
    2. Have the 4 wires from step 6: 1 and 3 about 170 long, 2 about 30 and 4 about 100, each with its socket.
    3. Find each piece's pocket.
    4. Slide all four in from the front, tab end first. Each should stay in.
    5. Turn the bay over: each single's tab shows in its recess.
    6. If a piece won't go in, or falls out, stop here.
    7. Take the two singles out. Tin each tab thinly, then slide all four back in.
    8. Strip 3 mm off each wire's joint end, twist, tin.
    9. Lay the bay on its front, on a cloth.
    10. Lay wires 1 and 2's bare ends flat on the + tab's outer side.
    11. Iron on the tab and both wires, 1 to 2 seconds. Hold still 3 seconds.
    12. Wait a minute, then wires 3 and 4 on the − tab, the same way.
    13. Meter: + plate to wires 1 and 2, − plate to wires 3 and 4, each near 0 Ω. + to − not near 0 Ω.

    Why now: everything that goes under it is in.

    1. Wires 1 and 3 out past the bay's bottom edge, 2 and 4 out past its top edge. Wire 4 runs up left of the step wires.
    2. Lower the bay flat onto its 3 posts. No wire on a post's top.
    3. 3 × M3 × 8 through its tabs.

    Hands: the pins stand 6 and 9 above the bay's top edge, in an opening 28 tall. A fingertip reaches; flat pliers fit.

    1. Wire 2, red, onto +. Wire 4, black, onto −.
    2. The jumper cap stays on.

    Why now: the bay is screwed down, so the lengths are final, and nothing after this pulls on them.

    1. Find the pads: BAT− beside D2, BAT+ beside D3. Check against Seeed's pinout.
    2. Wire 3, black, first: between the pin rows to BAT−. Cut 2 past the pad, strip 2, tin.
    3. Small bump of solder on the pad, wire on it, iron 2 to 3 seconds, hold still 3 seconds.
    4. Wire 1, red, to BAT+ the same way. No solder joining the two pads.
    5. Tape both wires to the clamp's top bar.
    6. Meter, no cells: BAT+ to the + contact near 0 Ω, BAT− to the − contact near 0 Ω, BAT+ to BAT− not near 0 Ω.
    1. Straight down: IN1's wire onto D7, IN2's onto D8, IN3's onto D9, IN4's onto D10.
    2. Wires 1 and 3 still lie flat between the rows.
    1. + contact to the ULN2003's + pin, and − contact to its − pin: near 0 Ω each.
    2. + contact to − contact: not near 0 Ω.
    3. Bench test, once there is firmware: two cells in, USB-C to load it; unplug, third cell in, step the motor with nothing on its shaft.

    Why now: the bridge screws onto the bay's boss, so the bay must be in. The drive isn't needed for measuring.

    1. Board onto the bridge: chip facing away, bottom corner holes on the pegs. Melt the peg tips over.
    2. Bridge onto the base, 2 × M3 × 8.
    3. Five whole jumpers.
    4. Sockets onto D0, D1 (orange), D4 (blue), D5 (green), GND (black).
    5. Flat along the bottom, up through the notch, along the channel: SDA nearest the upper wall, then SCL, VCC, VCC, GND.
    6. Mark each wire where it reaches its hole.
    7. Sockets off the XIAO, bridge unscrewed. The wires come with it.

    Why on the bench: the joints are on the chip side, which faces the dial once the bridge is in.

    1. Bridge front down, about 10 up (a vice or a block), chip side up.
    2. Cut each wire 3 past its mark and strip to the mark.
    3. Up through its hole until the insulation meets the board: 6 and 7 into VCC, 8 into SDA, 9 into SCL, 10 into GND.
    4. Wire 5, 25 of offcut, on the side without the chip: GND to DIR.
    5. Solder all five holes on the chip side. Trim to 1.2 or less: the sector passes 2.25 from them.
    6. Meter: VCC to GND not near 0 Ω, DIR to GND near 0 Ω, each socket to its hole near 0 Ω.
    7. Lay the wires back in the channel, under its fingers.
    1. The base onto the plate, held your way.
    2. Both side screws: the right one from the right side, the left one from the front with the hex key.
    1. Follow the fitting steps in cad/capstan_drive/v6/README.md. Tension the cord before the bridge goes on.
    2. Run it end to end about 20 times and take up the slack.
    1. Bridge on, its wires in the channel, 2 × M3 × 8.
    2. Sockets onto D0, D1 (orange), D4 (blue), D5 (green), GND (black).
    3. Tape the five as one flat bundle along the bottom.
    1. Cells in, by the + and − marks at each end.
    2. The cover, 2 × M3 × 6 down through its top face.
    3. The battery cover, slid on from the left, and its screw.
    4. The next day: tighten the sector's clamp screws once more.
